applicant_utility.summary: Funding here is not a scholarship you compete for separately - admission carries it, with the School paying all tuition and associated study fees and a stipend currently $50,000 per year - so the entire effort belongs in the application itself. The file is unusually short: transcripts, a personal statement and three letters, with no GRE and no minimum GPA, and roughly nine places a year from a worldwide pool. Apply by 1 December for the following autumn; if you later win an external fellowship such as NSF or NIH your stipend rises to $55,000 or the fellowship amount, whichever is higher.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Final-year students and recent graduates in any area of biology, or in computer science, engineering, mathematics, chemistry and physics, who want a small, mentorship-intensive biosciences PhD without writing a separate funding case.
application_readiness_checklist: Line up three recommenders early and brief them on your laboratory work, because letters are highly valued in the holistic review
Write the personal statement around concrete research experience and the challenges you have faced, since those are read explicitly
Check that your degree will actually be conferred before enrolment, as the School requires a bachelor's degree or equivalent by then
Only book TOEFL or IELTS if your previous university was not English-medium; the GRE is not required
Treat 1 December as a hard date and submit well before it, since review is tied to the annual cycle
Read the brochure and catalog as well as the How to Apply page, because the School points to them for process detail
common_rejection_risks: Weak or generic letters of recommendation, which the School says it values highly
A personal statement with no evidence of hands-on research or of obstacles overcome
Assuming a non-biology background is a barrier - it is not - while also failing to show genuine research engagement
Leaving English test scores until January if you come from a non-English-language university
Expecting a large cohort: with roughly nine students per entering class, admission is highly selective even though funding is automatic
Relying on grades alone: review is holistic and includes the types of courses you chose, so a non-linear path needs explaining, not hiding
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Visa and relocation costs beyond the published relocation support, and personal living expenses above the stipend; the School does not publish dependent or childcare costs.
document_audit: Transcripts may be unofficial at application, so do not wait for your registrar to issue sealed copies
The Graduate School page refers to official transcripts while the How to Apply page says unofficial - follow the application portal and be ready to send signed, sealed copies if accepted
Three letters are required, so choose referees who can speak to your research specifically rather than to your grades
There is no GRE requirement and no GPA minimum, so do not spend the autumn on test preparation instead of the statement
TOEFL or IELTS is only needed if your previous university was not English-medium, and no minimum score is published
alerts: Funding is automatic on admission, so there is no second application to win money - but equally no partial award to fall back on
1 December is the submission deadline for the current cycle and the application portal is labelled for the following year's intake
Holding an external fellowship raises the stipend to $55,000, or the fellowship amount if higher, so keep fellowship applications alive after admission
An annual educational enhancement fund covers meetings and courses, and first-year students are invited to live in the Knight House or Cutting House
The School also runs a separate BioAI PhD programme with its own rolling timeline, so check which programme fits your interests before applying
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the online application (transcripts, personal statement, three letters) by 1 December; the admission decision carries the tuition, stipend and support package automatically.
